words.enDefinition: friendly treatment or care offered to guests or visitors

examples.en: I was grateful for the hospitality my classmate's family showed me.
examples.zh: 我很感激同学一家对我的「热情款待」。

examples.en: She always remembers the hospitality she received during her first term.
examples.zh: 她一直记得自己第一学期受到的「热情款待」。

collocations: warm hospitality
enjoy someone's hospitality
appreciate your hospitality

words.enDefinition: someone staying temporarily as a visitor in another person's home

examples.en: My roommate made up the sofa for our houseguest that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，室友把沙发铺好给我们「留宿的客人」睡。

examples.en: I was a houseguest at a friend's flat during the reading break.
examples.zh: 阅读周假期，我是朋友公寓里的「留宿客人」。

collocations: welcome a houseguest
have a houseguest for the weekend
room for a houseguest

words.enDefinition: a person who visits without first arranging a particular time

examples.en: I had just put the kettle on when a drop-in visitor arrived.
examples.zh: 我刚烧上水，就来了一位「没预约就上门的访客」。

examples.en: Our group didn't mind a drop-in visitor joining us for tea sometimes.
examples.zh: 我们不介意偶尔有「没预约就上门的访客」加入，一起喝茶。

collocations: welcome a drop-in visitor
unexpected drop-in visitor
chat with a drop-in visitor

words.enDefinition: to think that people are coming to visit you

examples.en: We didn't expect company, so there were books all over the couch.
examples.zh: 我们「没想到会有客人来」，所以沙发上到处都是书。

examples.en: I told my roommate we might expect company after the afternoon seminar.
examples.zh: 我告诉室友，下午研讨课后可能「有客人要来」。

collocations: expect company this evening
expect company for dinner
expect company after lunch

words.enDefinition: to receive one or more people as guests in your home

examples.en: I love to have people over when our flat is free on Sundays.
examples.zh: 周日公寓空着的时候，我喜欢「请人来家里做客」。

examples.en: We can't usually have people over when everyone has exams the next week.
examples.zh: 要是大家下周都要考试，我们通常不方便「请人来家里做客」。

collocations: have people over for dinner
rarely have people over
like to have people over

words.enDefinition: to act as the person who welcomes and looks after visitors

examples.en: It was my turn to play host while my roommates were away.
examples.zh: 我室友都不在，这次轮到我「做东招待」。

examples.en: We offered to play host for three classmates who had just arrived.
examples.zh: 我们主动为刚到的三位同学「做东招待」。

collocations: play host to friends
take turns to play host
play host for the evening

words.enDefinition: to invite an arriving person to enter a place warmly

examples.en: A smile is an easy way to welcome someone in without saying much.
examples.zh: 不用多说，微微一笑就能「招呼对方进门」。

examples.en: It felt nice to welcome someone in when the hallway outside was cold.
examples.zh: 外面走廊挺冷的，「招呼对方进门」让人觉得暖心。

collocations: go to the door to welcome someone in
smile and welcome someone in
take a moment to welcome someone in

words.enDefinition: a friendly spoken invitation for a visitor to enter

examples.en: When my friend opened the door, she said, "Come on in. It's chilly outside."
examples.zh: 朋友打开门说：「快请进」，外面挺冷的。

examples.en: Come on in while I move these shoes away from the front door.
examples.zh: 「快请进」，我把门口这几双鞋挪开。

collocations: please come on in
come on in and sit down
come on in out of the cold

words.enDefinition: to enter a building without waiting for someone to open it

examples.en: You can let yourself in if I'm still busy with the laundry upstairs.
examples.zh: 要是我还在楼上忙着洗衣服，「你自己进来就好」。

examples.en: My roommate texted, "Let yourself in. We're both on the back porch."
examples.zh: 室友发消息说：「你自己进来就好」，我们俩都在后面的门廊上。

collocations: feel free to let yourself in
text someone to let yourself in
ask if you can let yourself in

words.enDefinition: offers to open the door when someone is waiting outside

examples.en: I'll get the door while you finish pouring the tea for our other guests.
examples.zh: 「我去开门」，你继续给其他客人倒茶吧。

examples.en: When the bell rang, I said, "I'll get the door. You can stay seated."
examples.zh: 门铃响时，我说：「我去开门」，你坐着就好。

collocations: don't worry, I'll get the door
I'll get the door this time
stay there, I'll get the door

words.enDefinition: to leave a door slightly open without closing it fully

examples.en: Could you leave the door ajar while I carry the mugs into the lounge?
examples.zh: 我把杯子拿到休息室的时候，你能「把门留条缝」吗？

examples.en: We chose to leave the door ajar so Dad could hear us from his chair.
examples.zh: 我们决定「把门留条缝」，这样爸爸坐在椅子上也能听到我们讲话。

collocations: ask someone to leave the door ajar
remember to leave the door ajar
agree to leave the door ajar briefly

words.enDefinition: welcomes a visitor who has managed to reach the location

examples.en: My friend laughed and said, "You found us! That entrance is hard to spot."
examples.zh: 朋友笑着说：「你找到我们这儿了」！那个入口挺不好找的。

examples.en: You found us. The building numbers on this street always confuse new visitors.
examples.zh: 「你找到我们这儿了」。这条街的门牌号老让初来的人看糊涂。

collocations: glad you found us
I'm glad you found us after all
you found us in the end

words.expression: did you find the place okay
words.lemma: did you find the place okay
words.enDefinition: asks a visitor whether they had trouble reaching the location
acceptedEnVariants: did you find the place okay

examples.en: Did you find the place okay? Some of the house numbers are hidden behind the trees.
examples.zh: 「这个地方好找吗」？有些门牌号被树挡住了。

examples.en: Our host asked, "Did you find the place okay?" and took our wet umbrellas at the door.
examples.zh: 主人在门口接过我们的湿雨伞，问：「这个地方好找吗」？

collocations: so did you find the place okay
did you find the place okay in the rain
ask if they found the place okay

words.expression: come in out of the rain
words.lemma: come in out of the rain
words.enDefinition: invites a visitor to come indoors to avoid getting wet
acceptedEnVariants: come in out of the rain

examples.en: Come in out of the rain while I grab a towel for your wet backpack.
examples.zh: 「快进来避避雨」，我去拿条毛巾擦擦你的湿书包。

examples.en: When my neighbour saw me outside, she said, "Come in out of the rain and have some tea."
examples.zh: 邻居见我在外面，就说：「快进来避避雨」，喝点茶吧。

collocations: please come in out of the rain
hurry and come in out of the rain
come in out of the rain first

words.enDefinition: offers to take a visitor's coat and put it away

examples.en: Can I take your coat? There are some hooks just behind the front door.
examples.zh: 「要我帮你挂外套吗」？大门后面有几个挂钩。

examples.en: My classmate asked, "Can I take your coat?" and hung it next to her own.
examples.zh: 同学问：「要我帮你挂外套吗」？随后把它挂在自己的外套旁。

collocations: here, can I take your coat
can I take your coat for you
can I take your coat while you find a seat

words.expression: where can I put my bag
words.lemma: where can i put my bag
words.enDefinition: asks where it is convenient to leave your bag
acceptedEnVariants: where can I put my bag

examples.en: Where can I put my bag while everyone tries to fit around the dining table?
examples.zh: 大家都要挤到餐桌边时，「我的包能放哪儿」？

examples.en: I arrived with my backpack and asked, "Where can I put my bag? It's quite heavy."
examples.zh: 我背着书包到了，问：「我的包能放哪儿」？还挺重的。

collocations: where can I put my bag for now
where can I put my bag while we eat
ask where I can put my bag

words.enDefinition: offers a visitor a place to put their belongings

examples.en: You can leave your things here while we clear a space for dinner.
examples.zh: 我们收拾餐桌准备开饭时，「东西可以放这儿」。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "Leave your things here," and cleared a spot on the bench.
examples.zh: 邻居说：「东西可以放这儿」，腾出了长凳上的一块地方。

collocations: you can leave your things here
feel free to leave your things here
just leave your things here for now

words.enDefinition: to clear a place for a visitor to put a coat

examples.en: Give me a second to make room for your coat before you sit down.
examples.zh: 你坐下之前稍等一下，我「给你的外套腾个地方」。

examples.en: My host said she would make room for your coat next to the kitchen door.
examples.zh: 主人说会在厨房门边「给我的外套腾个地方」。

collocations: let me make room for your coat
need to make room for your coat
make room for your coat on the rack

words.expression: where do you want my shoes
words.lemma: where do you want my shoes
words.enDefinition: asks a host where they prefer a visitor's shoes to go
acceptedEnVariants: where do you want my shoes

examples.en: Where do you want my shoes? I don't want to get mud on your clean floor.
examples.zh: 「鞋子放哪儿合适」？我不想把泥带到你干净的地板上。

examples.en: When my boots started dripping, I asked, "Where do you want my shoes for now?"
examples.zh: 靴子开始滴水时，我问：「鞋子暂时放哪儿合适」？

collocations: so where do you want my shoes
where do you want my shoes to go
ask where they want my shoes

words.enDefinition: a household request to remove shoes at the entrance

examples.en: The sign said "Shoes off at the door," so we left our boots on the mat.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「进门脱鞋」，我们就把靴子留在门垫上。

examples.en: My flatmate asked for shoes off at the door because the floor was freshly cleaned.
examples.zh: 地板刚清洁过，室友请大家「进门脱鞋」。

collocations: we prefer shoes off at the door
sign saying shoes off at the door
ask for shoes off at the door

words.expression: shall I take my shoes off
words.lemma: shall i take my shoes off
words.enDefinition: asks whether the host would prefer you to remove your shoes
acceptedEnVariants: shall I take my shoes off

examples.en: Shall I take my shoes off before walking on the rug in your living room?
examples.zh: 踩到你客厅的地毯之前，「我要脱鞋吗」？

examples.en: I looked down at the entrance mat and asked, "Shall I take my shoes off here?"
examples.zh: 我低头看看入口的门垫，问：「我在这儿要脱鞋吗」？

collocations: shall I take my shoes off here
shall I take my shoes off first
ask if I should take my shoes off

words.enDefinition: an extra set of indoor shoes kept for possible use

examples.en: There is a spare pair of slippers by the mat if your feet are cold.
examples.zh: 要是脚冷，门垫旁有一双「备用拖鞋」。

examples.en: The host brought a spare pair of slippers over from the shoe rack.
examples.zh: 主人从鞋架拿来了一双「备用拖鞋」。

collocations: offer a spare pair of slippers
lend a spare pair of slippers
keep a spare pair of slippers for guests

words.enDefinition: apologises informally because a place looks untidy to a visitor

examples.en: Pardon the mess. I had to finish a project before you came over.
examples.zh: 「屋里有点乱，见谅」。你来之前我得赶完一个项目。

examples.en: My friend said, "Pardon the mess," as she picked up her textbooks.
examples.zh: 朋友一边捡起课本，一边说：「屋里有点乱，见谅」。

collocations: please pardon the mess
pardon the mess in here
pardon the mess on the table

words.expression: have a seat wherever you like
words.lemma: have a seat wherever you like
words.enDefinition: invites a guest to sit anywhere they prefer
acceptedEnVariants: have a seat wherever you like

examples.en: Have a seat wherever you like while I go and find another mug for you.
examples.zh: 「想坐哪儿都行」，我去再给你找个杯子。

examples.en: Our host said, "Have a seat wherever you like," and pointed to the chairs by the window.
examples.zh: 主人指着窗边的椅子说：「想坐哪儿都行」。

collocations: please have a seat wherever you like
come in and have a seat wherever you like
go ahead and have a seat wherever you like

words.enDefinition: offers a soft supporting pillow to someone sitting down

examples.en: Would you like a cushion for the wooden chair, or are you comfortable there?
examples.zh: 木椅上「要个靠垫吗」？还是现在就坐得舒服？

examples.en: My neighbour asked, "Would you like a cushion?" when I chose the seat by the window.
examples.zh: 我选了窗边的位子时，邻居问：「要个靠垫吗」？

collocations: would you like a cushion for your back
would you like a cushion to sit on
ask if someone would like a cushion

words.enDefinition: invites someone to relax in a place where they are a guest

examples.en: Make yourself comfortable while I move the papers from this end of the sofa.
examples.zh: 「怎么舒服怎么来」，我把沙发这头的文件挪开。

examples.en: My friend's mum said, "Make yourself comfortable," and offered me the armchair.
examples.zh: 朋友妈妈说：「怎么舒服怎么来」，把扶手椅让给了我。

collocations: please make yourself comfortable
come in and make yourself comfortable
go ahead and make yourself comfortable

words.expression: I'll show you where everything is
words.lemma: i'll show you where everything is
words.enDefinition: offers to tell a visitor where they can find useful things
acceptedEnVariants: I'll show you where everything is

examples.en: I'll show you where everything is so you won't have to wake us up tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 「我带你看看东西在哪」，这样明早你就不用叫醒我们了。

examples.en: My friend said, "I'll show you where everything is," and opened the cupboard with the clean towels.
examples.zh: 朋友说：「我带你看看东西在哪」，打开了放干净毛巾的柜门。

collocations: come with me and I'll show you where everything is
first I'll show you where everything is
I'll show you where everything is when you arrive

words.expression: can I get you anything to drink
words.lemma: can i get you anything to drink
words.enDefinition: offers to fetch a drink for a visitor
acceptedEnVariants: can I get you anything to drink

examples.en: Can I get you anything to drink while we wait for my roommate to get back?
examples.zh: 等我室友回来的时候，「给你拿点喝的吗」？

examples.en: My friend's dad asked, "Can I get you anything to drink?" and held up two clean glasses.
examples.zh: 朋友爸爸举起两个干净杯子，问：「给你拿点喝的吗」？

collocations: can I get you anything to drink first
can I get you anything to drink while we wait
before we start, can I get you anything to drink

words.enDefinition: offers a choice between two common hot drinks

examples.en: Would you like tea or coffee while you wait for the others?
examples.zh: 等其他人的时候，你「喝茶还是喝咖啡」？

examples.en: My host asked, "Tea or coffee?" as she took down two mugs.
examples.zh: 主人一边拿下两个马克杯，一边问：「喝茶还是喝咖啡」？

collocations: would you like tea or coffee
offer someone tea or coffee
tea or coffee after dinner

words.expression: shall I put the kettle on
words.lemma: shall i put the kettle on
words.enDefinition: offers to heat water for tea or another hot drink
acceptedEnVariants: shall I put the kettle on

examples.en: It was cold outside, so I asked, "Shall I put the kettle on for tea?"
examples.zh: 外面挺冷，我就问：「我来烧点水泡茶吧」？

examples.en: Shall I put the kettle on while you show Lina where to hang her coat downstairs?
examples.zh: 你带莉娜去楼下挂外套时，「我来烧点水吧」？

collocations: say shall I put the kettle on
shall I put the kettle on for tea
shall I put the kettle on now

words.expression: how do you take your tea
words.lemma: how do you take your tea
words.enDefinition: asks how someone likes their tea, including milk or sugar
acceptedEnVariants: how do you take your tea

examples.en: My classmate asked, "How do you take your tea? I've got a little milk left."
examples.zh: 同学问：「你喝茶加些什么」？我还有一点牛奶。

examples.en: How do you take your tea at home? I can bring the sugar over if you like.
examples.zh: 你在家「喝茶加些什么」？你要是想加糖，我可以拿过来。

collocations: how do you take your tea again
so how do you take your tea
ask how someone takes their tea

words.enDefinition: politely says that you do not want sugar in your drink

examples.en: No sugar for me, please, but could I have a little milk in mine?
examples.zh: 「我这杯不加糖」，不过能加一点牛奶吗？

examples.en: When my host brought out the sugar, I said, "No sugar for me, thanks."
examples.zh: 主人拿糖出来时，我说：「我这杯不加糖」，谢谢。

collocations: no sugar for me, please
just milk and no sugar for me
I said no sugar for me

words.enDefinition: checks whether water from the tap is acceptable to a guest

examples.en: My host asked, "Is tap water okay?" before filling a jug for the table.
examples.zh: 主人往餐桌上的水壶装水之前问：「喝自来水可以吗」？

examples.en: Is tap water okay, or would you rather have something warm on a cold day?
examples.zh: 「喝自来水可以吗」？还是天冷，你想来点热的？

collocations: ask if tap water is okay
is tap water okay for you
is tap water okay with dinner

words.enDefinition: to pour more of a drink into a partly filled glass

examples.en: Shall I top up your glass while I've still got the jug here?
examples.zh: 水壶还在我手边，要不要我「给你续杯」？

examples.en: Let me top up your glass before I put the juice away.
examples.zh: 我先「给你续杯」，再把果汁收起来。

collocations: offer to top up your glass
shall I top up your glass
let me top up your glass

words.enDefinition: to place snacks where people can easily take them

examples.en: I offered to put out some snacks while my roommate went to meet our neighbours.
examples.zh: 室友去接邻居时，我主动说可以「摆点零食出来」。

examples.en: We decided to put out some snacks rather than cook a whole meal that evening.
examples.zh: 那天晚上，我们决定只「摆点零食出来」，不做一整顿饭。

collocations: offer to put out some snacks
put out some snacks for guests
remember to put out some snacks

words.enDefinition: a small amount of food offered when someone might be hungry

examples.en: Would you like a little something to eat now, or shall we wait until dinner?
examples.zh: 你现在想来「一点吃的」吗？还是等到晚饭？

examples.en: My friend fixed me a little something to eat when my train arrived late.
examples.zh: 我的火车晚点了，朋友给我弄了「一点吃的」。

collocations: get a little something to eat
offer a little something to eat
make a little something to eat

words.enDefinition: asks permission to use the bathroom in another person's home

examples.en: Can I use your bathroom before we leave to catch the last bus downtown?
examples.zh: 坐末班公交去市中心之前，「我能用一下洗手间吗」？

examples.en: I put down my bag and asked, "Can I use your bathroom for a moment?"
examples.zh: 我放下包问：「我能用一下洗手间吗」？

collocations: can I use your bathroom before I go
can I use your bathroom for a minute
ask if I can use your bathroom

words.expression: the bathroom is down the hall
words.lemma: the bathroom is down the hall
words.enDefinition: tells someone the bathroom is farther along a hallway
acceptedEnVariants: the bathroom is down the hall

examples.en: The bathroom is down the hall, just past the little shelf with everyone's shoes on it.
examples.zh: 「洗手间在走廊那头」，过了大家放鞋的小架子就是。

examples.en: My friend said, "The bathroom is down the hall, and the light switch is inside."
examples.zh: 朋友说：「洗手间在走廊那头」，灯的开关在里面。

collocations: the bathroom is down the hall on the left
the bathroom is down the hall from here
I think the bathroom is down the hall

words.enDefinition: asks where unused towels have been stored in a home

examples.en: Where are the clean towels? I brought a toothbrush, but I forgot to pack one.
examples.zh: 「干净毛巾放哪儿」？我带了牙刷，却忘了带毛巾。

examples.en: My cousin asked, "Where are the clean towels?" after putting her overnight bag upstairs.
examples.zh: 表姐把过夜行李放到楼上后问：「干净毛巾放哪儿」？

collocations: so where are the clean towels
where are the clean towels kept
do you know where the clean towels are

words.enDefinition: tells a guest that a spare blanket is available if needed

examples.en: There's an extra blanket on the chair if the room gets cold at night.
examples.zh: 要是晚上屋里冷，椅子上「还有一条备用毯子」。

examples.en: My friend said, "There's an extra blanket," and pointed to the bottom drawer.
examples.zh: 朋友指着最下面的抽屉说：「还有一条备用毯子」。

collocations: there's an extra blanket in the cupboard
there's an extra blanket if you need it
don't forget there's an extra blanket

words.enDefinition: to prepare a bed with sheets for someone who will sleep there

examples.en: My roommate offered to make up the spare bed while I picked up our visitor.
examples.zh: 我去接客人时，室友主动说会「把备用床铺好」。

examples.en: I just need to make up the spare bed before you bring your bag upstairs.
examples.zh: 你把包拿上楼之前，我只要先「把备用床铺好」。

collocations: offer to make up the spare bed
time to make up the spare bed
make up the spare bed for a guest

words.enDefinition: to sleep for the night on someone's sofa as a temporary arrangement

examples.en: I had to crash on the couch after missing the last train home.
examples.zh: 我没赶上回家的末班车，只能「临时在沙发上过夜」。

examples.en: My friends said I could crash on the couch if it got too late.
examples.zh: 朋友说，如果时间太晚，可以「临时在沙发上过夜」。

collocations: let someone crash on the couch
offer to let someone crash on the couch
need to crash on the couch

words.enDefinition: to sleep somewhere away from your own home for one night

examples.en: My sister decided to stay the night after we talked until midnight.
examples.zh: 我和妹妹聊到半夜，她决定「留宿一晚」。

examples.en: There's a spare bed if you'd rather stay the night and leave tomorrow.
examples.zh: 如果你想「留宿一晚」明天再走，这儿有张备用床。

collocations: offer to let someone stay the night
decide to stay the night
have someone stay the night

words.enDefinition: checks whether a visitor feels comfortable around dogs

examples.en: Are you okay with dogs? Ours usually sleeps near the chairs in the living room.
examples.zh: 「你介意家里有狗吗」？我家狗平时睡在客厅椅子旁。

examples.en: My neighbour asked, "Are you okay with dogs?" before inviting me into the garden.
examples.zh: 邻居请我进花园之前问：「你介意家里有狗吗」？

collocations: are you okay with dogs in the room
ask if they're okay with dogs
are you okay with dogs being here

words.enDefinition: asks someone to keep a cat from leaving the home

examples.en: Don't let the cat out when you bring your bag in through the back door.
examples.zh: 你从后门拿包进来时，「别让猫跑出去」。

examples.en: My classmate's only house rule was, "Don't let the cat out when you open the door."
examples.zh: 同学家就一个规矩，开门时「别让猫跑出去」。

collocations: please don't let the cat out
remember, don't let the cat out
don't let the cat out when you leave

words.expression: is it warm enough in here
words.lemma: is it warm enough in here
words.enDefinition: checks whether the temperature of a room is comfortable
acceptedEnVariants: is it warm enough in here

examples.en: Is it warm enough in here, or would you like me to turn the heating up?
examples.zh: 「屋里够暖和吗」？要不要我把暖气调高一点？

examples.en: My host asked, "Is it warm enough in here?" when I kept my sweater on indoors.
examples.zh: 我进屋没脱毛衣，主人问：「屋里够暖和吗」？

examples.zh: 「不用觉得欠我什么」。我已经有一本了，也知道你在收藏这些。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "Don't feel you owe me anything. I just thought you'd like this."
examples.zh: 邻居说：「不用觉得欠我什么」。我只是觉得你会喜欢。

collocations: please don't feel you owe me anything
really, don't feel you owe me anything
tell them don't feel you owe me anything

words.enDefinition: to give a gift in response to someone else's gift

examples.en: She said there was no need to give something in return just because she brought biscuits.
examples.zh: 她说，不用因为她带了饼干就「回送点东西」。

examples.en: I hoped to give something in return the next time my neighbours invited me over.
examples.zh: 我想下次邻居请我过去时，「回送点东西」。

collocations: feel you ought to give something in return
offer to give something in return
no need to give something in return

words.enDefinition: to contribute some money to a present shared with others

examples.en: Three of us offered to chip in toward a gift for the person hosting dinner.
examples.zh: 我们当中三个人提出「凑钱合送一份礼物」给晚饭的主人。

examples.en: I was happy to chip in toward a gift even though I couldn't be there.
examples.zh: 虽然没法到场，我也很乐意「凑钱合送一份礼物」。

collocations: agree to chip in toward a gift
ask who can chip in toward a gift
offer to chip in toward a gift

words.enDefinition: to go briefly to leave a present with someone

examples.en: I stopped by to drop off a gift for my neighbour after her exam.
examples.zh: 邻居考完试后，我「顺路把礼物送去」了。

examples.en: We planned to drop off a gift after class instead of mailing it.
examples.zh: 我们打算下课后「顺路把礼物送去」，就不寄了。

collocations: offer to drop off a gift
stop by to drop off a gift
arrange to drop off a gift

words.expression: can I help with the dishes
words.lemma: can i help with the dishes
words.enDefinition: offers to help wash dishes after sharing a meal
acceptedEnVariants: can I help with the dishes

examples.en: Can I help with the dishes before we leave to catch the train back home?
examples.zh: 我们去坐火车回家前，「我能帮忙洗碗吗」？

examples.en: I asked, "Can I help with the dishes?" when my friend started filling the sink.
examples.zh: 朋友开始往水槽里放水时，我问：「我能帮忙洗碗吗」？

collocations: can I help with the dishes after we eat
can I help with the dishes before I go
ask if I can help with the dishes

words.expression: you don't have to do the dishes
words.lemma: you don't have to do the dishes
words.enDefinition: reassures a guest that washing up is not their responsibility
acceptedEnVariants: you don't have to do the dishes

examples.en: You don't have to do the dishes. I'll put them in the dishwasher after you leave.
examples.zh: 「你不用洗碗」。等你走了我会把它们放进洗碗机。

examples.en: My host said, "You don't have to do the dishes. Go and talk to the others."
examples.zh: 主人说：「你不用洗碗」，去和其他人聊天吧。

collocations: you don't have to do the dishes today
don't worry, you don't have to do the dishes
you don't have to do the dishes this time

words.enDefinition: to take spare clothes for changing into when staying somewhere

examples.en: I'm going to bring a change of clothes in case I stay the night.
examples.zh: 万一我要留宿，我打算「带一身换洗衣服」。

examples.en: My neighbour told me to bring a change of clothes for the next morning.
examples.zh: 邻居叫我「带一身换洗衣服」，第二天早上穿。

collocations: remember to bring a change of clothes
tell someone to bring a change of clothes
need to bring a change of clothes

words.enDefinition: a room in a home where visitors can sleep

examples.en: My friend's parents offered me their guest room when the trains stopped.
examples.zh: 列车停运时，朋友的父母留我睡他们的「客房」。

examples.en: We moved two boxes out of the guest room before she arrived.
examples.zh: 她到之前，我们从「客房」里搬走了两个箱子。

collocations: stay in the guest room
get the guest room ready
spare pillows in the guest room

words.enDefinition: an extra toothbrush kept in case someone needs one

examples.en: My friend offered me a spare toothbrush because I hadn't planned to stay.
examples.zh: 我本来没打算留宿，朋友就给了我一支「备用牙刷」。

examples.en: There's a spare toothbrush in this drawer if you forgot to pack yours.
examples.zh: 如果你忘了带牙刷，这个抽屉里有支「备用牙刷」。

collocations: offer a spare toothbrush
keep a spare toothbrush
have a spare toothbrush for guests

words.enDefinition: to place a towel where a visitor can use it

examples.en: I'll put a towel out so you don't have to look for one.
examples.zh: 我会「拿条毛巾放好」，省得你自己找。

examples.en: My roommate offered to put a towel out for my sister before she arrived.
examples.zh: 妹妹到之前，室友说可以为她「拿条毛巾放好」。

collocations: remember to put a towel out
offer to put a towel out
put a towel out for a guest

words.enDefinition: lets someone know they need not worry about disturbing your sleep

examples.en: Don't worry about waking me if you need to leave for the station early.
examples.zh: 如果你要早早去车站，「不用怕把我吵醒」。

examples.en: My host said, "Don't worry about waking me when you make breakfast in the morning."
examples.zh: 主人说：「早上你做早餐时，不用怕把我吵醒」。

collocations: really, don't worry about waking me
please don't worry about waking me
don't worry about waking me up

words.expression: feel free to use the kitchen
words.lemma: feel free to use the kitchen
words.enDefinition: gives a guest permission to use the host's kitchen
acceptedEnVariants: feel free to use the kitchen

examples.en: Feel free to use the kitchen if you get back later than us this evening.
examples.zh: 今晚如果你回来得比我们晚，「厨房可以随便用」。

examples.en: My neighbour said, "Feel free to use the kitchen," and showed me where she kept the mugs.
examples.zh: 邻居说：「厨房可以随便用」，还告诉我她平时把杯子放在哪儿。

collocations: please feel free to use the kitchen
feel free to use the kitchen in the morning
tell guests to feel free to use the kitchen

words.enDefinition: gives a visitor permission to get a drink for themselves

examples.en: Help yourself to a drink while I finish helping the neighbours with their bags.
examples.zh: 「想喝什么自己拿」，我先帮邻居把包拿完。

examples.en: My friend said, "Help yourself to a drink. The cold glasses are in the fridge."
examples.zh: 朋友说：「想喝什么自己拿」。冰过的杯子在冰箱里。

collocations: please help yourself to a drink
go ahead and help yourself to a drink
feel free to help yourself to a drink

words.enDefinition: to give someone space to continue what they are doing alone

examples.en: I'll leave you to it while you call your family from the spare room.
examples.zh: 你在备用房间给家人打电话，我就不打扰了，「让你自己忙」。

examples.en: I should leave you to it so you can get ready before everyone arrives.
examples.zh: 我先不打扰了，「让你自己忙」，大家到之前你还能准备一下。

collocations: I'll leave you to it
probably best to leave you to it
happy to leave you to it

words.enDefinition: to walk with a departing guest as far as the door

examples.en: My host always gets up to see someone to the door when the evening ends.
examples.zh: 晚上的活动结束时，主人总会站起来「送客人到门口」。

examples.en: I went to see someone to the door and nearly forgot to return their umbrella.
examples.zh: 我去「送人到门口」，差点忘了把雨伞还给对方。

collocations: offer to see someone to the door
go to see someone to the door
get up to see someone to the door

words.expression: I'll walk you to the bus stop
words.lemma: i'll walk you to the bus stop
words.enDefinition: offers to accompany a departing visitor as far as their stop
acceptedEnVariants: I'll walk you to the bus stop

examples.en: I'll walk you to the bus stop so you don't have to find it in the dark.
examples.zh: 「我陪你走到公交站」，免得你天黑了还得自己找。

examples.en: My friend said, "I'll walk you to the bus stop," before she went to find her jacket.
examples.zh: 朋友去找夹克前说：「我陪你走到公交站」。

collocations: wait and I'll walk you to the bus stop
come on, I'll walk you to the bus stop
if you like, I'll walk you to the bus stop

words.enDefinition: tells the host they need not accompany you to the exit

examples.en: I can show myself out. You can stay here and finish talking to your guests.
examples.zh: 「我自己出去就行」。你可以留在这儿继续跟客人聊。

examples.en: I said, "I can show myself out," and put my coat on in the hallway.
examples.zh: 我说：「我自己出去就行」，在走廊里穿上了外套。

collocations: don't get up, I can show myself out
thanks, I can show myself out
no need to come, I can show myself out

words.enDefinition: to stay longer than a host wants or is comfortable with

examples.en: It's easy to overstay your welcome when you lose track of the time.
examples.zh: 聊得忘了时间，很容易「待得太久惹人嫌」。

examples.en: You might overstay your welcome if you ignore the host's bedtime routine.
examples.zh: 要是不留意主人的睡觉时间，就可能「待得太久惹人嫌」。

collocations: try not to overstay your welcome
worry that you'll overstay your welcome
easy to overstay your welcome

words.enDefinition: asks whether your visit is preventing someone from going to bed

examples.en: Are we keeping you up? I didn't realise it was already past eleven o'clock.
examples.zh: 「我们耽误你睡觉了吗」？我没意识到已经十一点多了。

examples.en: My roommate asked, "Are we keeping you up?" when our friend started to yawn.
examples.zh: 朋友开始打哈欠时，室友问：「我们耽误你睡觉了吗」？

collocations: sorry, are we keeping you up
are we keeping you up too late
wait, are we keeping you up

words.expression: we should let you get some rest
words.lemma: we should let you get some rest
words.enDefinition: signals you are about to leave so someone can rest
acceptedEnVariants: we should let you get some rest

examples.en: We should let you get some rest. You've been taking care of everyone all evening.
examples.zh: 「我们该让你休息了」。你一晚上都在照顾大家。

examples.en: When our host said she was tired, I said, "We should let you get some rest."
examples.zh: 主人说累了，我就说：「我们该让你休息了」。

collocations: I think we should let you get some rest
right, we should let you get some rest
maybe we should let you get some rest

words.enDefinition: expresses regret that your group has to leave a visit soon

examples.en: Sorry we can't stay longer. I've got to meet my lab partner before the last bus.
examples.zh: 「抱歉我们不能多待」。我得在末班车前见一下实验搭档。

examples.en: I said, "Sorry we can't stay longer," as my sister and I put on our coats.
examples.zh: 妹妹和我穿外套时，我说：「抱歉我们不能多待」。

collocations: really sorry we can't stay longer
sorry we can't stay longer today
we're sorry we can't stay longer

words.expression: text me when you get home
words.lemma: text me when you get home
words.enDefinition: asks a departing person to message you once they arrive home
acceptedEnVariants: text me when you get home

examples.en: Text me when you get home so I know you caught the last train okay.
examples.zh: 「到家给我发消息」，好让我知道你顺利坐上了末班车。

examples.en: My friend said, "Text me when you get home," just before I got on the bus.
examples.zh: 就在我上公交车前，朋友说：「到家给我发消息」。

collocations: remember to text me when you get home
just text me when you get home
can you text me when you get home

words.expression: I'll keep it here for you
words.lemma: i'll keep it here for you
words.enDefinition: an offer to look after something until its owner can collect it
acceptedEnVariants: I'll keep it here for you

examples.en: “I'll keep it here for you,” my host wrote after finding the blue scarf.
examples.zh: 主人找到那条蓝围巾后写道：“「我先替你收着」。”

examples.en: “I'll keep it here for you until next weekend,” my friend said at the door.
examples.zh: 朋友在门边说：“下周末前，「我先替你收着」。”

collocations: don't worry, I'll keep it here for you
I'll keep it here for you until Friday
I'll keep it here for you until you return

words.enDefinition: to give a visitor somewhere to stay for a short time

examples.en: We could put someone up on the sofa if the buses stopped running.
examples.zh: 如果公交停运，我们能「让人在家留宿」，睡沙发。

examples.en: It's easier to put someone up now that the spare room is cleared.
examples.zh: 现在备用房间收拾出来了，「让人在家留宿」容易多了。

collocations: offer to put someone up
agree to put someone up
put someone up for the weekend

words.enDefinition: thanks someone for letting you stay in their home

examples.en: Thanks for putting me up. Otherwise I would have missed the morning lecture.
examples.zh: 「谢谢你让我留宿」。不然我肯定赶不上早上的大课。

examples.en: I sent her a message saying, "Thanks for putting me up," after the early train.
examples.zh: 我坐早班火车离开后，给她发了条消息：「谢谢你让我留宿」。

collocations: and thanks for putting me up
thanks for putting me up last night
thanks for putting me up at such short notice

words.expression: you made me feel right at home
words.lemma: you made me feel right at home
words.zhGloss: 你让我像在自己家一样
words.enDefinition: thanks a host for making a visit especially comfortable
acceptedZhAnswers: 你让我像在自己家一样
acceptedEnVariants: you made me feel right at home

examples.en: You made me feel right at home, especially when you remembered how I liked my tea.
examples.zh: 「你让我像在自己家一样」，尤其是你还记得我喜欢怎么喝茶。

examples.en: I told my classmates, "You made me feel right at home," before leaving their flat that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚离开同学的公寓前，我对他们说：「你们让我像在自己家一样」。

collocations: honestly, you made me feel right at home
right away, you made me feel right at home
thank you, you made me feel right at home

words.expression: please thank your family for me
words.lemma: please thank your family for me
words.enDefinition: asks someone to pass your thanks on to their family
acceptedEnVariants: please thank your family for me

examples.en: Please thank your family for me. I felt very welcome at your house last night.
examples.zh: 「请替我谢谢你家人」。昨晚在你家，我感觉很受欢迎。

examples.en: I texted, "Please thank your family for me," after getting back to my place that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚回到自己住处后，我发消息说：「请替我谢谢你家人」。

collocations: and please thank your family for me
please thank your family for me when you see them
while you're there, please thank your family for me

words.enDefinition: repeats your thanks to someone who gave you a meal

examples.en: Thanks again for dinner and for making sure I got to the station.
examples.zh: 「再次谢谢你请我吃饭」，还特意照应我到车站。

examples.en: I wrote, "Thanks again for dinner," under the photo my friend took at her flat.
examples.zh: 我在朋友家拍的照片下面写了句「再次谢谢你请我吃饭」。

collocations: anyway, thanks again for dinner
by the way, thanks again for dinner
thanks again for dinner last night

words.enDefinition: promises to tell another person that someone has thanked them

examples.en: I'll pass on your thanks when I see my parents at their place tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我明天去看父母时，「会转达你的谢意」。

examples.en: My friend replied, "I'll pass on your thanks. My sister loved having everyone over."
examples.zh: 朋友回复：「我会转达你的谢意」。我妹妹特别喜欢大家来做客。

collocations: don't worry, I'll pass on your thanks
of course I'll pass on your thanks
I'll pass on your thanks when I see her

words.enDefinition: a written card thanking the person who looked after you

examples.en: We left a thank-you card for the host on the table before catching our train.
examples.zh: 我们去坐火车之前，在桌上留了张「写给主人的感谢卡」。

examples.en: Everyone signed a thank-you card for the host after the group stayed at her place.
examples.zh: 一行人借住在她家后，每个人都在「写给主人的感谢卡」上签了名。

collocations: write a thank-you card for the host
leave a thank-you card for the host
sign a thank-you card for the host

words.enDefinition: to give a person unusually attentive or affectionate treatment

examples.en: You don't have to make a fuss over someone just because they're visiting for dinner.
examples.zh: 别人来吃顿饭，你用不着「对人家格外上心」。

examples.en: My friend said she didn't want us to make a fuss over someone on her birthday.
examples.zh: 朋友说，她生日那天不想我们「对她格外上心」。

collocations: tend to make a fuss over someone
try not to make a fuss over someone
make a fuss over someone who is visiting

words.expression: is there somewhere I can change
words.lemma: is there somewhere i can change
words.enDefinition: asks whether a private place is available to change clothes
acceptedEnVariants: is there somewhere I can change

examples.en: Is there somewhere I can change? My jeans got soaked on the walk from the bus.
examples.zh: 「有地方让我换衣服吗」？从公交站走过来时，我的牛仔裤湿透了。

examples.en: Is there somewhere I can change before we leave for the concert? I brought another shirt.
examples.zh: 去听音乐会之前，「有地方让我换衣服吗」？我带了另一件衬衫。

collocations: is there somewhere I can change first
is there somewhere I can change before dinner
ask if there's somewhere I can change
